title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: the notes interpret the absolute Galois group E_{K̄/K} of a finitely generated field K over Q through the exact sequence (8) 1 → π_{K̄/K} → E_{K̄/K} → Γ_{K̄/K} → 1. Here Γ_{K̄/K} = Gal(Q̄/k), where k is the algebraic closure of Q in K (a number field, called K_0 on the previous page). The kernel π_{K̄/K} = Gal(K̄/KQ̄) is the 'geometric' part.

On the previous page K is written as the direct limit of its finitely generated Q-subalgebras A_i. One may take a cofinal system of regular A_i, so that the U_i = Spec A_i are smooth, with transition maps given by localisations (open immersions).

This page:
(i) Following M. Artin, one may even take the U_i to be 'elementary' schemes over k, i.e. towers of elementary fibrations in curves (Artin's 'bons voisinages', SGA4 XI).
(ii) The U_i are geometrically connected, even geometrically irreducible, over k, because k is algebraically closed in K. Spec K = η is their common generic point.
(iii) A choice of K̄ gives a geometric point η̄ over all the U_i, hence groups E_i = π_1(U_i, η̄). Since Spec K = lim U_i, the standard limit theorem (SGA1 / SGA4 VII, passage to the limit for étale covers) gives (10): E_{K̄/K} = π_1(η, η̄) ≅ lim_i E_i.
(iv) Set Ū_i = U_i ⊗_k Q̄. For each i the homotopy exact sequence (SGA1 IX 6.1, valid for U_i quasi-compact and geometrically connected over k) gives (12): 1 → π_i = π_1(Ū_i, η̄) → E_i → Gal(Q̄/k) → 1. These form a projective system of extensions with constant quotient.
(v) Next page: passing to the limit recovers (8), with π_{K̄/K} = lim π_i. The π_i can be computed transcendentally as profinite completions of π_1(U_i(C)). For Artin elementary U_i, each π_i is a successive extension of n free profinite groups of finite rank, where n = tr.deg K/Q.

Purpose: this is the setting for birational anabelian geometry in the 'Longue Marche' programme. The Galois group of a function field over a number field is presented as a pro-object of fundamental groups of good models, each an extension of the arithmetic Galois group by a geometric group of 'elementary' (iterated free) type.
errors: Notational slip: the marginal note to (10) says Γ_i = π_1(U_i, η̄), but in the text that group is E_i. Γ is otherwise reserved for the arithmetic quotient.
The common quotient is called Γ' in the text, but it is Γ_{Q̄/k} = Γ_{K̄/K} as defined just above. This is a harmless notational inconsistency.

Minor gap: Spec K = lim U_i, and hence (10), holds for the full system or any cofinal subsystem. Restricting to Artin elementary U_i requires that they form a cofinal system of neighbourhoods of η. This is true (good neighbourhoods exist around any point of a smooth variety over a field of characteristic 0, so in particular around the generic point), but it is used implicitly.

ideas.what: Absolute Galois group of a function field as the projective limit of étale fundamental groups of its smooth affine models
ideas.modern_name: π_1 of the generic point = lim π_1 of open neighbourhoods; Galois group of a function field as a pro-system of fundamental groups
ideas.where_published: SGA1 (V, IX), SGA4 VII/IX; also used in Esquisse d'un programme / Longue Marche

ideas.what: Use of Artin's elementary fibrations (iterated fibrations in curves) as a cofinal system of models
ideas.modern_name: Artin neighbourhoods / good neighbourhoods (bons voisinages); K(π,1) property
ideas.where_published: SGA4 XI (Artin), cited in the anabelian context in the Esquisse/Longue Marche

ideas.what: Homotopy exact sequence 1 → π_1(Ū) → π_1(U) → Gal(Q̄/k) → 1 for geometrically connected U over k, forming a projective system with fixed quotient
ideas.modern_name: Fundamental exact sequence of étale fundamental groups

ideas.what: Geometric fundamental groups computed transcendentally as profinite completions of topological π_1 via an embedding K̄ → C
ideas.modern_name: Riemann existence / comparison theorem for π_1

deep.surprise_reason: This is a clean, standard set-up for birational anabelian geometry, assembled from SGA1/SGA4 results and Artin's good neighbourhoods. It is well known and essentially what appears in the Esquisse and in the anabelian literature (Pop, Mochizuki, Nakamura). It contains no new result or unexplored connection.

In the line under (12), the last term is most plausibly 'Γ_{K̄/K} = Γ_{Q̄/k} = Γ_k' (the arithmetic quotient), not 'Γ_[?]'.
In (10) the right-hand side reads 'lim_i E_i'; a struck-through letter precedes E_i in the image.
The crossed-out word before k is 'Kar' (probably the beginning of a symbol, abandoned); the following text reads 'sur k (clôture alg. de Q dans K)'.
